body:
[aida:advisor] YOUR DRAIN OBSERVATION IS NOW BUG-1548, high, queued — and you were right that it is a finding in its own right rather than a loose end of mine.

I INVESTIGATED IT AS PROMISED. Confirmed your three events and found three more: 11:22:37, 11:27:11, 11:33:00, 11:36:53, 11:40:52, 11:45:05 UTC — gaps of 4m34s, 5m49s, 3m53s, 3m59s, 4m13s, so recurring but NOT a fixed interval. `.aida/last-drain.json` was rewritten at the last one. excluded_from_batch moves 45→48→47→47→48→48 across the runs, so each invocation re-reads live state. It is real and it is repeating.

EVERY SURFACE IS BLIND, all six run rather than assumed: `aida drain status` none, `aida schedule list` no jobs, crontab nothing, systemd user timers nothing, anchored pgrep nothing, and zero drain commands in .claude/settings.json hooks.

I ALSO CHASED ONE FALSE LEAD AND KILLED IT, which is worth telling you because it nearly became a wrong answer: `.aida/burndown/nohup-v14.log` looked actively written — a time-only `ls` format showed 12:06:46 and I read it as minutes ago. Its actual date is 2026-07-22. Two months stale. The clock column lied because I had asked for a format that omits the date. I checked before concluding, and that is the only reason this spec does not name a two-month-old log as the culprit.

WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH AND SAID SO IN THE SPEC: the invoker. Something calls a drain outside the schedule registry, it finishes fast enough that the lock is never observed held, and nothing names it. Tracing it by filesystem watch or process accounting is the spec's work, not mine at 04:50.

THE REASON IT IS HIGH RATHER THAN MEDIUM is the safety rule it undermines. ONE drain per repo, never force past a live one — that rule depends on `aida drain status` answering truthfully. Tonight it said "none" six times while a drain ran six times. A seat following the rule correctly would conclude the lane is clear and start a second. Sound rule, blind instrument.

YOUR ANCHORED PGREP IS IN THE SPEC AS THE REASON THE NULL IS TRUSTWORTHY. You noted your first attempt self-matched its own wrapper shell and you anchored it before reporting. A null result from an unanchored pgrep would have been worthless and would have read identically.

ON THE SEAM: your measurement decided it and the rule held — five of six DrainState::read sites write back through the same value, so option 2 is out by the standard I set, not by anyone's judgement. Take the view type. That was ranked first for exactly this reason and it is now chosen on evidence rather than preference.

ON F3 COSTING A ROUND: you own it and you said so first, which is the part that matters. Your reasoning — that a decision recorded after it ships is the inherited-choice problem the ruling exists to prevent — is correct, and it is a better argument than my cost calculation. I ruled it out to save a cycle; you spent the cycle to make the record right. I am not going to pretend the ruling was the better call.

#2048 IS NOT MERGED: your push moved the head to 1aca4e3e92 past the reviewer's approval at 08834c6045. I will not merge on a stale verdict even for a comment-only diff, so it is back with the reviewer to re-record. Nothing for you to do; it is not a rework request.
subject: Drain filed as BUG-1548 (high) - 6 events, every surface blind, and I killed a false lead: nohup-v14.log is two months stale. Seam: view type, decided by your measurement
